contents.html: The Information Technology Laboratory (ITL) at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) promotes the U.S. economy and public welfare by providing technical leadership for the Nation’s measurement and standards infrastructure. ITL develops tests, test methods, reference data, proof of concept implementations, and technical analyses to advance the development and productive use of information technology. ITL’s responsibilities include the development of management, administrative, technical, and physical standards and guidelines for the cost-effective security and privacy of other than national security-related information in Federal information systems.
contents.html_ja: 米国国立標準技術研究所（NIST）の情報技術研究所（ITL）は、国の計測・標準インフラに対する技術的なリーダーシップを提供することで、米国経済と公共の福祉を促進しています。ITL は、情報技術の開発と生産的な利用を進めるため、テスト、テスト手法、参照データ、概念実証実装および技術分析を開発しています。ITL の責務には、連邦情報システムにおける国家安全保障に関連しない情報のセキュリティとプライバシーを費用対効果の高い形で確保するための、管理上、行政上、技術上および物理的な標準およびガイドラインの策定が含まれます。

contents.html: FIPS 201-2 requires explicit user action by the Personal Identity Verification (PIV) cardholder as a condition for use of the digital signature key stored on the card. This document clarifies the requirement for explicit user action to encourage the development of compliant applications and middleware that use the digital signature key.

contents.html: 1. Introduction
contents.html_ja: 1. はじめに
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p6の章見出し

contents.html: Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 201 defines the Personal Identity Verification (PIV) Card and supporting process requirements. A private cryptographic key, the digital signature key (DSK), is specified for digitally signing messages and data. The DSK is generated on the card and is never exported; all operations with this private key are performed by the PIV Card. FIPS 201 requires authentication of the cardholder via “explicit user action” each time the DSK is used to perform a cryptographic operation.
contents.html_ja: 連邦情報処理標準（FIPS）201 は、個人識別情報確認（PIV）カードと、それを支えるプロセスの要件を定めています。秘密の暗号鍵である電子署名鍵（DSK）は、メッセージやデータに電子署名するために規定されています。DSK はカード上で生成され、エクスポートされることはありません。この秘密鍵を用いる操作はすべて PIV カードが実行します。FIPS 201 は、DSK を使って暗号操作を行うたびに、「明示的なユーザー操作」によってカードホルダーを認証することを求めています。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p6: 1章の3段落が1ブロックになっていた。段落に分ける

contents.html_ja: NIST Special Publication 800-73 は、要求された暗号操作ごとに個人識別番号（PIN）がカードに送信されることを確実にするため、DSK のアクセス条件として「PIN ALWAYS」を規定しています。しかし FIPS 201 は、PIN 入力パッドを内蔵したカードリーダーの使用を義務付けていません。その結果、PIV カード自体は、新たに入力された PIN と、呼び出し元のアプリケーションまたはシステムがキャッシュした PIN を区別できません。
contents.html: NIST Special Publication 800-73 specifies the “PIN ALWAYS” access condition for the DSK to ensure that the Personal Identification Number (PIN) is submitted to the card for each requested cryptographic operation. However, FIPS 201 does not mandate the use of card readers with integrated PIN entry pads. As a result, the PIV Card itself cannot differentiate between a freshly supplied PIN and a PIN cached by the calling application or system.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p6: 1章の3段落が1ブロックになっていた。段落に分ける

contents.html_ja: 本仕様は、一貫した信頼できるレベルのセキュリティを確保するため、「明示的なユーザー操作」の要件を明確にし、この要件を満たす実装オプションの範囲を規定します。
contents.html: This specification clarifies the requirement for “explicit user action” and specifies a range of implementation options that satisfy this requirement, in order to ensure a consistent and reliable level of security.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p6: 1章の3段落が1ブロックになっていた。段落に分ける

contents.html: 2. Background
contents.html_ja: 2. 背景
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p6の章見出し

contents.html: The digital signature key (DSK) is intended to sign data, such as electronic forms, documents or electronic mail. Operations using the DSK can be performed after the PIV Card has been activated. To protect the DSK against misuse after activation, each subsequent private key operation requires an explicit user action.
contents.html_ja: 電子署名鍵（DSK）は、電子フォーム、文書、電子メールなどのデータに署名するためのものです。DSK を使う操作は、PIV カードが有効化された後に実行できます。有効化の後に DSK が不正に使われるのを防ぐため、以降の秘密鍵操作ごとに明示的なユーザー操作が必要です。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p6: 2章の4段落が1ブロックになっていた。段落に分け、脚注番号1を上付きに、斜体を付ける

contents.html_ja: PIV カードには、カードホルダーの認証と明示的なユーザー操作の表明の両方に使う単一の仕組み、すなわちユーザー PIN の入力が組み込まれています。<sup>1</sup> ユーザー PIN は、カードを特権操作／保護された操作のために有効化するとき、または DSK による署名操作を行うときに、PIV カードに提示しなければなりません。ユーザーに PIN の入力が求められ、その値が操作ごとに PIV カードに提示される場合、明示的なユーザー操作の要件は明らかに満たされています。これにより、署名生成操作が行われるたびに、ユーザーがその場にいて DSK で署名を生成する意図があることが保証されます。ただし、署名操作ごとにユーザーが PIN を再入力することを確実にするには、PIV カードの境界の外側にあるシステムレベルの管理策が必要です。
contents.html: The PIV Card incorporates a single mechanism for both authenticating the cardholder and expressing explicit user action: entry of the user PIN.<sup>1</sup> The user PIN must be presented to the PIV Card to activate the card for privileged/protected operations or to perform a signing operation with the DSK. If the user is prompted for the PIN, and that value is presented to the PIV Card for each operation, the requirement for explicit user action is clearly satisfied. This ensures that the user is present and intended to generate a signature with the DSK each time a signature generation operation is performed. However, ensuring that the PIN is re-entered by the user for each signature operation requires system level controls outside the boundaries of the PIV Card.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p6: 2章の4段落が1ブロックになっていた。段落に分け、脚注番号1を上付きに、斜体を付ける

contents.html_ja: 加えて、アプリケーションによっては、署名のたびにカードホルダーへ PIN の入力を求めるのは現実的でないと考えられます。たとえば、ポリシーによりすべての電子メールに署名することをユーザーに求める場合があります。ユーザーが短時間に大量の電子メールを送信するとき、PIN を繰り返し入力するとユーザビリティが大きく低下します。このような場合、アプリケーションまたはミドルウェアは、スマートカードの PIN を保持（キャッシュ）し、ユーザーに代わって提示するように設計できます。しかし、PIN をキャッシュすると、アプリケーションまたはミドルウェアがカードホルダーに知られることなく PIN を提示できてしまう可能性があります。
contents.html: In addition, for some applications it is considered impractical to require the cardholder to enter the PIN for each signature. For example, users may be required by policy to sign every email message. When the user is sending a large number of email messages in a short period, repeatedly entering the PIN greatly decreases usability. In such cases, the application or middleware can be designed to retain (or cache) the smart card PIN and present it on behalf of the user. However, caching the PIN may allow the application or middleware to present the PIN without the cardholder’s knowledge.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p6: 2章の4段落が1ブロックになっていた。段落に分け、脚注番号1を上付きに、斜体を付ける

contents.html_ja: 以降の各節では、DSK を使うシステムで考えられるアーキテクチャを示し、DSK の PIN ALWAYS アクセス条件における明示的なユーザー操作となる最小限のセキュリティ目標と管理策を定義します。
contents.html: The following sections identify possible architectures for systems that use the DSK, and define the minimum security objectives and controls that constitute explicit user action for the PIN ALWAYS access condition of the DSK.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p6: 2章の4段落が1ブロックになっていた。段落に分け、脚注番号1を上付きに、斜体を付ける

contents.html: <sup>1</sup> FIPS 201-2 introduces the option for PIV Cards to implement on-card fingerprint biometric comparison, in addition to the PIN, as a mechanism to authenticate the cardholder to the card; however, the recommendations in this document only apply to the PIN.
contents.html_ja: <sup>1</sup> FIPS 201-2 では、PIV カードが、カードに対してカードホルダーを認証する仕組みとして、PIN に加えてカード上での指紋バイオメトリック照合を実装するオプションが導入されました。ただし、本書の推奨事項が適用されるのは PIN のみです。

contents.html: 3. Architectures
contents.html_ja: 3. アーキテクチャ
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p7の章見出し

contents.html: There are two basic configurations for a PIV compliant system that leverages the DSK:
contents.html_ja: DSK を利用する PIV 準拠システムには、基本的な構成が 2 つあります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p7: 導入文と番号付きの構成(1)(2)を分ける

contents.html_ja: PIN がオペレーティングシステム、ミドルウェアまたはアプリケーションに一切公開されないように、コンピューティングシステムを設計できます。このシステムの構成要素は、キーパッド付きの外付けスマートカードリーダーを備えたホストコンピュータと、PIV カードです。この場合、PIN はユーザーから PIV カードへ「直接」送信されます。アプリケーションやオペレーティングシステムは PIN をキャッシュできないため、PIN ALWAYS の要件を強制すれば、DSK の秘密鍵操作ごとの明示的なユーザー操作を確認するのに十分です。
contents.html: A computing system can be designed so that the PIN is never exposed to the operating system, middleware, or applications. The components of this system are the host computer with an external smart card reader with keypad, and the PIV Card. In this case, the PIN is submitted from the user “directly” to the PIV Card. FIPS 201-2 requires explicit user action by the Personal Identity Verification (PIV) cardholder as a condition for use of the digital signature key stored on the card. This document clarifies the requirement for explicit user action to encourage the development of compliant applications and middleware that use the digital signature key.
personal identification number; personal identity verification; PIN caching; PIV
4.2 Explicit User Action with PIN Caching — 2

Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 201 defines the Personal Identity Verification (PIV) Card and supporting process requirements. A private cryptographic key, the digital signature key (DSK), is specified for digitally signing messages and data. The DSK is generated on the card and is never exported; all operations with this private key are performed by the PIV Card. FIPS 201 requires authentication of the cardholder via “explicit user action” each time the DSK is used to perform a cryptographic operation. NIST Special Publication 800-73 specifies the “PIN ALWAYS” access condition for the DSK to ensure that the Personal Identification Number (PIN) is submitted to the card for each requested cryptographic operation. However, FIPS 201 does not mandate the use of card readers with integrated PIN entry pads. As a result, the PIV Card itself cannot differentiate between a freshly supplied PIN and a PIN cached by the calling application or system. This specification clarifies the requirement for “explicit user action” and specifies a range of implementation options that satisfy this requirement, in order to ensure a consistent and reliable level of security.

The digital signature key (DSK) is intended to sign data, such as electronic forms, documents or electronic mail. Operations using the DSK can be performed after the PIV Card has been activated. To protect the DSK against misuse after activation, each subsequent private key operation requires an explicit user action. The PIV Card incorporates a single mechanism for both authenticating the cardholder and expressing explicit user action: entry of the user PIN.1 The user PIN must be presented to the PIV Card to activate the card for privileged/protected operations or to perform a signing operation with the DSK. If the user is prompted for the PIN, and that value is presented to the PIV Card for each operation, the requirement for explicit user action is clearly satisfied. This ensures that the user is present and intended to generate a signature with the DSK each time a signature generation operation is performed. However, ensuring that the PIN is re-entered by the user for each signature operation requires system level controls outside the boundaries of the PIV Card. In addition, for some applications it is considered impractical to require the cardholder to enter the PIN for each signature. For example, users may be required by policy to sign every email message. When the user is sending a large number of email messages in a short period, repeatedly entering the PIN greatly decreases usability. In such cases, the application or middleware can be designed to retain (or cache) the smart card PIN and present it on behalf of the user. However, caching the PIN may allow the application or middleware to present the PIN without the cardholder’s knowledge. The following sections identify possible architectures for systems that use the DSK, and define the minimum security objectives and controls that constitute explicit user action for the PIN ALWAYS access condition of the DSK.

1 FIPS 201-2 introduces the option for PIV Cards to implement on-card fingerprint biometric comparison, in addition to the PIN, as a mechanism to authenticate the cardholder to the card; however, the recommendations in this document only apply to the PIN.

There are two basic configurations for a PIV compliant system that leverages the DSK: (1) A computing system can be designed so that the PIN is never exposed to the operating system, middleware, or applications. The components of this system are the host computer with an external smart card reader with keypad, and the PIV Card. In this case, the PIN is submitted from the user “directly” to the PIV Card. The application or operating system cannot cache the PIN so enforcing the PIN ALWAYS requirement is sufficient to confirm explicit user action for each DSK private key operation. (2) A computing system can be designed so that the PIN is entered via the host computer’s keyboard. The components of this system are the host computer system with an internal or external smart card reader without keypad, and the PIV Card. In this case, the PIN is entered into the keyboard and is processed by the operating system, middleware, or
application before submission to the PIV Card.

In configuration (1), it is the external reader’s responsibility to ensure that the PIN is supplied to the PIV Card as a result of an explicit action. In configuration (2), the host system software, in combination, has the responsibility to ensure that the PIN is supplied to the PIV Card as a result of an explicit action. The following section specifies implementation guidelines for PIV system components.

This section specifies minimum security controls and objectives for system implementations that leverage the DSK to ensure that each presentation of the PIN represents an explicit user action. Section 4.1 describes functional requirements for systems that prohibit PIN caching. Section 4.2 specifies the minimum security objectives and controls for system implementations that support DSK PIN caching.

Entering the PIN each time is the most direct and strongest mechanism to achieve explicit user action for the PIN ALWAYS access condition of the DSK. This can be achieved by any of the following methods: (1) PIN entry is performed exclusively using an external card reader with key pad,2 and the

card reader itself does not cache the PIN; or (2) PIN entry is performed using the host system, and the operating system, middleware, and all applications are configured so that the PIN is never cached. In combination with the PIV Card’s native controls, both solutions confirm user action for each
DSK private key operation simply by enforcing the PIN ALWAYS requirement.
4.2 Explicit User Action with PIN Caching

If the PIN is cached by any component of the system, it is the system’s responsibility to ensure an explicit user action occurs before the PIN is presented to the PIV Card. Examples of affirmative action could include clicking “OK” in a pop-up box or by user selection of an appropriate menu option or commit button within the application. PIN caching implementations for the DSK should ensure that the following are satisfied:
2 Note that the card reader needs to intercept and discard any Application Protocol Data Units (APDUs) that contain the PIN originating from the host system.

The PIN cache is limited to a single process or application instance. That is, a PIN presented by an email application to digitally sign email is not accessible to other applications resident on the host system, such as workflow or document signing applications.
The cached PIN is not presented to the smart card without an associated explicit user action. The explicit user action may be handled by either of the following methods:

a. The component that confirms the explicit user action is the component that caches the PIN (e.g., the application or the middleware); or b. The programming interface between the component that confirms the explicit user action and the component that caches the PIN can convey the difference between a request associated with explicit user action and a request that was not associated with an explicit user action.
The PIN cache is cleared if any of the following conditions apply:

a. The system is shut down or rebooted; b. The PIV Card is removed from the system; c. The associated process or application instance is terminated; or d. The PIN has not been presented to the PIV Card for more than N minutes. (In other words, more than N minutes have passed since the user performed an explicit action authorizing a signature.) The value of N is an agency (or Identity, Credential, and Access Management Subcommittee—ICAMSC) decision but should not exceed thirty minutes.
